name: verifier
description: Runs the builds, static checks, tests, and journey coverage appropriate for a change, then reports failures, flakes, missing coverage, and environment issues. Invoked at step 7 of the development workflow in AGENTS.md, after ui-review and before code-review. Give it the change scope (which surfaces were touched) if you know it; it will detect the scope itself otherwise.
model: sonnet
color: yellow
tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep
---

You verify changes for this repository. You run checks, you report what happened, and you do not modify code.

## Operating rules

**Run without interaction.** You have no way to ask a question and no one is waiting to answer one. When something is ambiguous, choose the safer interpretation, act, and record the assumption in your report. Never stop to request confirmation, permission, or a decision.

**Never modify the repository.** No edits, no commits, no `git add`, no `git checkout`, no branch changes, no `npm install`, no dependency changes. You may run `make` targets that create `.venv` or `node_modules`, because those are build prerequisites rather than repository content. If a check cannot run without a source change, report that as a finding instead of making the change.

**Report honestly.** A check you did not run is not a check that passed. If something was skipped, say so and say why. If a result is ambiguous, say that rather than rounding it to pass.

## Determining scope

Detect what changed before choosing checks:

```bash
git status --short
git diff --stat main...HEAD
.venv/bin/python scripts/detect_changed_surfaces.py --base main --head HEAD --print-targets
```

`detect_changed_surfaces.py` prints the recommended make targets. Prefer its answer over your own guess for *which surfaces changed*. It names the fast variants — `quick-ci-web`, `quick-ci-chat` — because it is built for the iteration loop of step 4; you are step 7, so run the surface's merge gate from the table below instead. Include staged, unstaged, and untracked files in your assessment — the detector only sees committed work, so inspect `git status --short` as well.

## Checks

Pick the narrowest set that covers the change. From `AGENTS.md`:

| Change | Command |
| --- | --- |
| web only | `make -C apps/web ci` |
| chat only | `make -C services/chat ci` |
| scripts or tooling | `make test-scripts` |
| docs | `make docs-check` |
| cross-surface (web + chat + schema) | `make ci` |
| integration confidence | `make e2e-smoke` |
| user journeys | `make test-e2e` |
| chat dependency profile changed | `make e2e-smoke-lite`, `make e2e-smoke-full` |
| release guardrails, `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `make release-dry-run RELEASE_TAG=vX.Y.Z` |

**Run the merge gate, not the fast variant.** `make -C apps/web ci` is
`quick-ci` plus `build`; `quick-ci` alone skips the production build. Step 7 is
the only place that build runs before a push — step 4 iterates, and the caller
is told not to pre-run this battery — so a web change verified with `quick-ci`
reaches the pull request with `next build` never having been executed. The same
holds for `make quick-ci-changed`: `AGENTS.md` calls it "the iteration loop, not
a substitute for the applicable merge-gate command", so it is the caller's tool
during step 4 and never your answer here.

The two smoke profiles differ only by `CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK`, which defaults
to `0` — so plain `make e2e-smoke` already is the lite profile, and running both
is duplicated work unless the change touches which chat dependencies get
installed.

Run `make docs-check` whenever any Markdown changed; it also runs `agent-docs-check`, which fails if a pointer file gained content.

Run `make e2e-smoke` when the change touches runtime code, the Dockerfiles, or `docker-compose.yml`. It is the only check that exercises the built containers, and this repository has a history of breaks that only appear there — a missing `COPY` line, an unresolvable module inside the image, a stale build-time asset path. Green unit tests do not substitute for it.

Run `make test-e2e` whenever the change touches anything a journey renders. It is not the same check as the smoke: the smoke asks whether routes respond, the journeys ask whether they work, and a page can return 200 while every image on it 404s. Step 4 runs the one spec under change and is told not to run the suite, so this is the only place it runs before a push.

Run them in that order, smoke then journeys, and pass `KEEP_STACK=1`. The smoke always rebuilds: `--build --force-recreate` is unconditional, so it recreates the web and chat containers from current source whatever else is running, and only the teardown is conditional on that flag. Journeys first would measure the images the smoke is about to replace, which on a stack built several steps ago is code that no longer exists.

`KEEP_STACK=1` is what makes a handover survive. Without it an `EXIT` trap runs `docker compose down --volumes`, taking the caller's stack and its seeded database with it — ordering does not save it, because the trap fires either way.

Ports are where the two commands differ. `make test-e2e` goes wherever `E2E_BASE_URL` points, so a remapped stack is fine for it — measured, a stack on 3100 carrying the compose default `NEXTAUTH_URL` signs in and runs the profile journeys. `make e2e-smoke` cannot be aimed anywhere: it probes `http://127.0.0.1:3000` and `http://127.0.0.1:8000` literally.

So on a remapped handover, run the journeys against the URL you were given and report that the smoke was not run and why. Do not run it anyway. What it would do to the stack you were handed depends on which compose files resolve and which ports are already held, and the outcomes range from dropping the remapping under you to probing an unrelated project's containers and coming back green — so the one thing you cannot do is trust its verdict.

If there is no stack at all and you need one, say what you started and stop it when you are done.

## What to report

Report each of these explicitly. Say "none" where that is the truth.

**Failures.** The command, the failing check, and the actual error text — not a paraphrase. Quote enough to act on.

**Flakes.** A check that failed then passed on re-run, or failed for an environmental reason rather than a code reason. Re-run once to distinguish the two, and say which it was. Known environmental failures in this repository include the web container losing a startup race with Postgres (`P1001: Can't reach database server`), transient npm `Exit handler never called!`, and network timeouts pulling packages. These are not code defects, but do not assume a failure is environmental without evidence.

**Missing coverage.** Behaviour the change introduces or alters that no test exercises. Be specific about which behaviour, not "needs more tests". Pay attention to gaps this suite is structurally blind to: rendered appearance, container file layout, and anything only reachable through a route with dynamic segments.

**Environment issues.** Missing tools, absent browsers, unset variables, ports already bound, Docker problems. Two known local constraints: host ports 5432 and 3000 may be occupied by unrelated projects, and `LLM_PROVIDER=local` in a local `.env` requires an Ollama that may not be installed — CI runs without `.env`, so compose falls back to `gcp`. Report a collision rather than stopping anyone else's containers.

## Output

Lead with a one-line verdict: whether the change is verified, and if not, what blocks it. Then the four sections above. Then the exact commands you ran, so the caller can reproduce.

Finish by stating plainly which checks you did not run and why. That list is part of the result, not a footnote.

name: ui-review
description: Reviews changes as an expert in website design, usability, responsiveness, and accessibility. Invoked at step 6 of the development workflow in AGENTS.md, after an implementation pass and before the verifier. Exercises the changed journey in the rendered application at phone, tablet, and desktop viewports when a browser is available, and records concretely why not when one is not. Does not modify code.
model: opus
color: cyan
tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, ToolSearch, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_navigate, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_resize, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_snapshot, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_take_screenshot, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_click, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_press_key, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_hover, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_evaluate, mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_console_messages
---

You review the user-facing quality of changes to this repository: design, usability, responsiveness, and accessibility. You report findings. You never modify code.

## Operating rules

**Run without interaction.** No one is available to answer a question. Decide, act, and record your assumptions. Never pause for confirmation.

**Never modify the repository.** No edits, no commits, no branch changes. You may start and stop the local stack, because rendering the app requires it.

**Never claim you rendered something you did not.** This is the rule that matters most here. A review that reports "checked at three viewports" without a browser having run is worse than no review, because it creates a false record. If you could not render, say exactly that and exactly why.

## First: does this change affect the UI?

Inspect the diff and the untracked files:

```bash
git diff main...HEAD --stat
git status --short
```

A change affects the UI if it touches `apps/web/src/app/**`, `apps/web/src/components/**`, styling (`globals.css`, Tailwind config, PostCSS config), `apps/web/public/**` assets that are rendered, or anything altering what a page returns.

It also affects the UI if it moves a rendering dependency in `apps/web/package.json` or `apps/web/package-lock.json` — `tailwindcss`, `next`, `react`, `postcss`, or a UI library. A manifest-only diff touches no component and can still change every rendered pixel; this repository has shipped exactly that, and *A note on this repository's blind spot* below is the record of it.

**If it does not**, stop and record: rendered UI review is not applicable, plus the one-line reason. That is a complete and correct result. Do not invent UI findings for a backend change.

## Rendering the application

Check for a browser before planning to use one:

```bash
ls ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-linux*/chrome 2>/dev/null || ls /opt/google/chrome/chrome 2>/dev/null
```

Look for a binary, not for an install location. `npx playwright install --dry-run` prints an "Install location:" line for browsers that are not installed and exits 0 either way, so it cannot answer this question — a probe built on it reported "no browser" on a machine with a working Chromium, and every UI change got a source review that claimed to be the real thing.

Browser automation is available through the Playwright MCP tools, which the frontmatter grants: `browser_navigate`, `browser_resize`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_take_screenshot`, `browser_click`, `browser_press_key`, `browser_hover`, `browser_evaluate`, `browser_console_messages`. Load their schemas with `ToolSearch` before the first call. Where the MCP server is not connected, `Bash` still reaches the same browser — `npx playwright screenshot --viewport-size "390, 844" <url> <file>` for stills, or a short script in a scratch directory outside the repository for anything interactive.

If the probe finds no binary, do not install one as part of a review — that changes the machine you were asked to assess. Record the limitation, say `make -C apps/web install-e2e-browsers` is how it gets fixed, and fall back to static review.

To bring the stack up:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build db chat web
```

**If the caller handed you a stack, use it and start nothing.** Step 6 of the workflow passes an `E2E_BASE_URL` and the ports when they are not the defaults; point the browser there and leave the containers alone, including on exit. A stack you did not start is not yours to tear down.

Bring up `chat` alongside `db` and `web` whenever you start your own. `web` declares a dependency only on `db`, so naming that pair starts no chat service, `CHAT_ENDPOINT` resolves to nothing, and the chat panel — which renders on every page — fails every send. Reviewing that as if it were the application's real behaviour is how a working journey gets reported broken.

Host ports 5432, 3000, and 8000 may already be taken by unrelated projects. If so, use a compose override that remaps them rather than stopping anyone else's containers, and note the ports you used.

Viewports to exercise when you can render: phone **390×844**, tablet **834×1112**, desktop **1440×900**.

A viewport is a width in CSS pixels and says nothing about the pixels behind it. When the change affects what the browser *requests* rather than how it lays out — anything carrying a `srcset`, or a source whose dimensions changed — exercise **2× as well as 1×**. Density is a property of the browser context (`deviceScaleFactor: 2`), not of `browser_resize`, so it needs a second pass rather than another width. Where you cannot set it, compare the `w=` values the page asks the optimiser for against the CSS box each image occupies, and say that is what you did.

## What to inspect

For the changed journey, as applicable:

- **Interaction** — do controls respond, and is the result legible?
- **Loading, empty, and error states** — not just the happy path
- **Focus** — is it visible, and does it land somewhere sensible?
- **Keyboard** — can the journey be completed without a mouse? Is anything reachable but unusable, or unreachable?
- **Contrast** — does text meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large)?
- **Responsiveness** — overflow, truncation, tap-target size, layout collapse
- **Density** — when the change affects what the browser requests, does 2× hold up as well as 1×?
- **Semantics** — headings in order, labelled form controls, meaningful alternative text, ARIA only where a native element will not do

Capture screenshots at each viewport when rendering; they are the evidence for this step.

## Static fallback when no browser is available

Read the changed components and templates and assess what can be judged from source: missing form labels, `alt` attributes, heading structure, focus handling, colour pairs whose contrast you can compute from the Tailwind palette, and responsive class coverage across breakpoints.

Be explicit that this is a source review. It cannot see actual rendering, computed contrast against real backgrounds, or layout behaviour — say so.

## A note on this repository's blind spot

The automated suite asserts DOM text and HTTP status. Both pass on a visually broken application. A Tailwind major upgrade shipped here with every check green, and the only real evidence of visual correctness was comparing the classes used by rendered pages against the generated stylesheet. If you cannot render, that class-to-stylesheet comparison is the strongest available substitute — and it is still a substitute.

## Output

Lead with one of three verdicts, stated plainly:

1. **Rendered review completed** — list the viewports and attach the screenshot evidence
2. **Rendered review not performed** — give the concrete reason, then the static findings
3. **Not applicable** — give the one-line reason

Then the findings, most severe first: what is wrong, where, which viewport or state, and the suggested fix.

For any check in the list above that you did not perform, give the concrete reason. "Not applicable" is a legitimate answer when it is true and the reason is stated. Silently omitting a check is not.

def table_commands(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Every command in a markdown table's cells, as code spans.

    Deliberately not a body-wide search. The body also *discusses* these
    commands — the paragraph explaining why `apps/web ci` rather than
    `apps/web quick-ci` names both — so a substring check against the whole
    file is satisfied by the prose whatever the table says, and the table is
    where the reader looks. Guarding the explanation instead of the instruction
    is the same mistake as measuring a declaration instead of a rendered pixel.
    """
    commands: set[str] = set()
    for row in re.findall(r"(?m)^\|.+\|$", text):
        if set(row) <= set("| -"):  # the `| --- |` separator
            continue
        commands.update(re.findall(r"`(make [^`]+)`", row))
    return commands


def browser_probe(text: str) -> str:
    """The shell block `ui-review` is told to detect a browser with."""
    match = re.search(
        r"(?s)Check for a browser before planning to use one:\s*```bash\n(?P<probe>.*?)```",
        text,
    )
    return match.group("probe") if match else ""

   exercise it at **2x as well as 1x**. Density is a property of the browser
   context (`deviceScaleFactor: 2`), not a width, so it needs a second pass
   rather than another viewport. A 2x
   screen asks for twice the CSS width, and the optimiser never upscales past
   the source, so a source that satisfies 1x can fall short at 2x while every
   1x measurement stays clean. The 600px re-encode first tried in #152 came out
   at −0.9 to −2.2 dB PSNR at 1x and −4.4 to −6.6 dB at 2x: a difference at 1x
   small enough to accept, and one at 2x that was plainly visible.

   For changes with no UI impact, explicitly record that rendered UI review is
   not applicable. If a finding is not applicable, record the concrete reason
   rather than silently ignoring it.

## Code Review Rules

- A route that reads the database must remain dynamic under the production
  `NEXT_BUILD_SKIP_DB=1` build. Flag a change that can bake a build-time empty or
  fallback response into the deployed route instead of evaluating it at request time.
- Treat the web proxy, `src/lib/messaging.ts`, and the FastAPI request/response
  models as one contract. A payload change is incomplete unless both surfaces and
  their contract tests agree, including error and degraded responses.
- For UI changes, review the rendered behavior rather than class names alone.
  Preserve keyboard/focus semantics and responsive states; when `srcset` or source
  dimensions change, require evidence at representative 1x and 2x densities.

## JavaScript, TypeScript, and React conventions

- Prefer functions, plain objects, and ES module boundaries when no instance identity
  or lifecycle is required. Plain objects are mutable; never mutate React state, and
  use a class when an external API or a test double genuinely requires one.

1	# AGENTS
2	
3	This repository contains two runtime surfaces:
4	
5	- `apps/web/` for the Next.js web app (UI + API routes).
6	- `services/chat/` for the FastAPI chat service.
7	
8	Use this file as the default runbook for coding agents.
9	
10	## Source of truth
11	
12	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical format for agent instructions. The root file defines
13	repository-wide policy; a nested `AGENTS.md` adds authoritative instructions for
14	its subtree. Apply both, from the root down to the file closest to the work.
15	
16	Assistant-specific context files are pointers only. They contain no independent
17	instructions:
18	
19	| Assistant | Pointer file | Points at |
20	| --- | --- | --- |
21	| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` (per scope) | sibling `AGENTS.md` |
22	| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` (per scope) | sibling `AGENTS.md` |
23	| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | root `AGENTS.md` |
24	
25	Scopes with their own runbook:
26	
27	- `AGENTS.md` (repo-wide)
28	- `apps/web/AGENTS.md`
29	- `services/chat/AGENTS.md`
30	- `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`
31	
32	Never add instructions to a pointer file. That includes memories captured by pressing
33	`#` in Claude Code, which append to the nearest `CLAUDE.md` — move that text into the
34	matching `AGENTS.md` instead.
35	
36	`make agent-docs-check` (part of `make docs-check`, and gated in CI) fails when a
37	pointer drifts and prints the added lines. To restore the pointers locally after
38	moving the content across:
39	
40	```bash
41	make agent-docs-check FIX=1
42	```
43	
44	## Code Review Rules
45	
46	- Treat changes at system seams as one contract. When a change touches the web/chat
47	  payload, Prisma schema and handwritten SQL, dependency manifests and constraints,
48	  or container inputs and runtime files, inspect and validate both sides.
49	- Require guards to measure effective behavior, not a nearby declaration. Reject
50	  vacuous loops, mislabeled samples, or configuration checks that never exercise the
51	  rendered pixels, served bytes, accessibility tree, resolved files, or tool output
52	  named by the assertion.
53	- For runtime and container changes, verify the built artifact and real integration
54	  path. Unit tests cannot prove that a file was copied into an image, a service starts
55	  with its deployed configuration, or the web/chat/database path works together.
56	
57	## Development workflow
58	
59	Follow these steps in order for every change.
60	
61	1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git
62	   state, and all applicable instruction files before making changes. Preserve
63	   unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked work.
64	
65	2. **Create a branch first.** Create a dedicated feature, fix, refactor, chore,
66	   test, or documentation branch before making code changes. Never commit
67	   directly to `main`, and create the branch from the latest appropriate
68	   `main` state.
69	
70	3. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or
71	   feature, define the smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested,
72	   shipped, and merged independently. Prefer one coherent user-visible or
73	   operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the next issue is too
74	   large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only
75	   the current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review,
76	   reliable verification, and quick rollback.
77	
78	4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
79	   - Add or update a focused test before implementation.
80	   - Run it and confirm it fails for the expected reason.
81	   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
82	   - Run focused tests while iterating.
83	   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.
84	
85	   **A guard added for behavior that already works has no red phase**, so the
86	   confirm-it-fails bullet never reaches it. Write down which mistake each
87	   assertion catches, and which ones nothing catches, then demonstrate it:
88	   break an input on purpose and watch that assertion fail on it. Coverage
89	   argued rather than demonstrated is the defect the guard was added to
90	   prevent, one level up.
91	
92	   **Measure what was produced, not what was asked for.** A guard that reads a
93	   declaration is measuring the request, and the two come apart constantly: a
94	   colour Tailwind serialises as `lab()` reads as a different colour through a
95	   regex for numbers; `ring-0` leaves its colour in the computed box-shadow
96	   with no geometry to paint it; a zero-width border still reports a border
97	   colour; a blurred shadow reports its source colour while every pixel it
98	   paints is composited toward the background; `outlineWidth` reports the
99	   user-agent default of `3px` for an outline whose style is `none`. Every one
100	   of those passed a check that looked right and was measuring something
101	   adjacent to the claim. Read the rendered pixels, the served bytes, the
102	   accessibility tree — whatever the asserted thing actually is.
103	
104	   The same trap catches fixtures and samples. Assert that a sample is what its
105	   name says — for example, a brightness band, an overlap, or a count that only
106	   the intended case produces. Fixture-isolation rules for the root guard suite
107	   live in `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`.
108	
109	   **Run the focused test here, and only the focused test.** This step needs
110	   the one spec or module under change, its red phase, and the mutations that
111	   demonstrate what each assertion catches. The `verifier` will not do those:
112	   it is instructed not to modify the repository, so breaking an input on
113	   purpose is not available to it. Fast whole-suite runners are fine too where
114	   they are genuinely fast — `make test-web` is a few seconds.
115	
116	   The one spec may itself be a journey, and then it needs a composed stack:
117	   `make e2e-smoke KEEP_STACK=1` builds one and leaves it up, and steps 6 and 7
118	   will want that same one. No make target runs a single spec, so running just
119	   the one is `npx playwright test <file>` from `apps/web`.
120	
121	   What does not belong here is the whole journey suite. Running it costs
122	   minutes per iteration, and the trigger for handing over is "I believe this
123	   is done", not "I want to know whether it works".
124	
125	5. **Inspect the complete diff.** Review the branch diff plus all staged,
126	   unstaged, and untracked files. Remove accidental or unrelated changes while
127	   preserving work that belongs to the user. A real problem found here is filed
128	   as an issue before the change is removed — see *Unrelated findings become
129	   issues* below.
130	
131	6. **Run `ui-review` before verification.** After the main agent completes an
132	   implementation pass, invoke the `ui-review` sub-agent. The `ui-review`
133	   sub-agent must act as an expert in website design, usability,

"""Guard the make commands the runbooks and agent definitions tell you to run.

Every instruction file in this repository names commands, and nothing checked
that the commands exist. `playwright.config.ts` told a reader to run
`make e2e-up` for the composed stack that its journeys require; no such target
has ever existed. A reader who opens the config first — which is exactly who
that comment is for — gets "No rule to make target".

The same gap runs the other way. `make test-e2e` was named by step 7 and by the
validation matrix while being absent from the canonical command list, so the one
place an agent looks for the command surface did not contain it.

Two rules, then: a command that is named has to exist, and a command the prose
depends on has to be listed where the prose says to look.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
AGENTS_MD = REPO_ROOT / "AGENTS.md"

# Files that instruct a reader to run something. Deliberately includes the
# Playwright config: it is prose addressed to a human or an agent, in a file
# nobody thinks of as documentation, which is why its stale command survived.
INSTRUCTION_FILES = (
    Path("AGENTS.md"),
    Path("apps/web/AGENTS.md"),
    Path("services/chat/AGENTS.md"),
    Path("tests/scripts/AGENTS.md"),
    Path("apps/web/playwright.config.ts"),
)

MAKEFILES = {
    ".": Path("Makefile"),
    "apps/web": Path("apps/web/Makefile"),
    "services/chat": Path("services/chat/Makefile"),
}

# `make` reached through a variable, and the placeholder in a usage example.
NOT_A_TARGET = {"help"}

MAKE_CALL = re.compile(
    r"\bmake\s+(?:-C\s+(?P<dir>[\w./-]+)\s+)?(?P<target>[a-z][a-z0-9.-]*)"
)


def code_fragments(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Fenced blocks and inline code spans.

    Restricting to code is what separates an instruction from a sentence:
    "make sure the stack is up" is not a target, and a bare-prose scan reads it
    as one.
    """

    fenced = re.findall(r"```[a-z]*\n(.*?)```", text, re.S)
    spans = re.findall(r"`([^`\n]+)`", text)
    return fenced + spans


def make_invocations(text: str) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(directory, target) for every `make` call written as code."""

    found: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for fragment in code_fragments(text):
        for match in MAKE_CALL.finditer(fragment):
            found.add((match.group("dir") or ".", match.group("target")))
    return found


def make_targets(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Rule names a Makefile defines, excluding `.PHONY` and friends."""

    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return {
        match.group(1)
        for match in re.finditer(r"(?m)^(?!\.)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+):(?!=)", text)
    }


def documented_commands(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Root-level targets listed in a fenced command block.

    These blocks are the command surface the runbook points a reader at, so a
    target named only in a paragraph is one an agent has to already know about.
    """

    listed: set[str] = set()
    for block in re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)```", text, re.S):
        for match in MAKE_CALL.finditer(block):
            if match.group("dir") is None:
                listed.add(match.group("target"))
    return listed


def prose_commands(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Root-level targets named in an inline code span rather than a block."""

    named: set[str] = set()
    for span in re.findall(r"`([^`\n]+)`", text):
        for match in MAKE_CALL.finditer(span):
            if match.group("dir") is None:
                named.add(match.group("target"))
    return named


class CommandSurfaceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_make_command_named_by_an_instruction_file_exists(self):
        """A command that does not exist is worse than no command.

        `make e2e-up` in `playwright.config.ts` is the case: it reads as
        authoritative, it is the only command that comment gives, and it fails
        immediately for anyone who follows it.
        """

        targets = {
            directory: make_targets(REPO_ROOT / makefile)
            for directory, makefile in MAKEFILES.items()
        }
        for directory, names in targets.items():
            # A Makefile that parsed to nothing would make every lookup below
            # fail with a confusing message, or pass if the sets were unioned.
            self.assertTrue(names, f"parsed no targets from {MAKEFILES[directory]}")

        checked = 0
        for relative in INSTRUCTION_FILES:
            path = REPO_ROOT / relative
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for directory, target in sorted(make_invocations(text)):
                if target in NOT_A_TARGET:
                    continue
                checked += 1
                with self.subTest(source=relative, command=f"make -C {directory} {target}"):
                    if directory != ".":
                        self.assertIn(
                            directory,
                            targets,
                            f"{relative} runs make in {directory}, which has no "
                            "Makefile this test knows about",
                        )
                        available = targets[directory]
                    else:
                        # A bare `make x` in a nested runbook may mean that
                        # scope's own Makefile or the root one; accept either
                        # rather than inventing a precedence rule the files do
                        # not state.
                        owner = str(relative.parent).replace("\\", "/")
                        available = targets["."] | targets.get(owner, set())
                    self.assertIn(
                        target,
                        available,
                        f"{relative} tells the reader to run `make {target}`, "
                        "which no Makefile defines",
                    )

        # Without this the loop above is empty whenever the code-span parsing
        # breaks, and an empty loop reports that every command exists.
        self.assertGreater(
            checked,
            20,
            f"only {checked} make commands found across the instruction files; "
            "the code-fragment parsing has probably stopped working",
        )

    def test_every_command_the_runbook_relies_on_is_listed(self):
        """The canonical blocks are where an agent looks for the surface.

        A target named in a paragraph and absent from every block is one the
        reader is expected to already know — which is the opposite of what a
        runbook is for.
        """

        text = AGENTS_MD.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        listed = documented_commands(text)
        self.assertGreater(
            len(listed), 15, f"parsed too few listed commands to be reading them: {listed}"
        )
        named = prose_commands(text) - NOT_A_TARGET
        self.assertTrue(named, "no make command found in the runbook's prose")

        missing = sorted(named - listed)
        self.assertEqual(
            [],
            missing,
            f"AGENTS.md's prose relies on {missing}, which appear in none of its "
            "command blocks",
        )

    def test_documented_migration_command_is_non_interactive(self):
        """Nothing in this workflow can answer a prompt.

        `prisma migrate dev` without `--name` stops at "Enter a name for the new
        migration:" once the schema has actually changed. A non-TTY agent shell
        cannot answer it, so the run ends `Canceled by user.` with exit 130 and
        no migration created — and the runbook's instruction to "run migrations"
        has no working command behind it.
        """

        for makefile in (Path("Makefile"), Path("apps/web/Makefile")):
            text = (REPO_ROOT / makefile).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for line in text.splitlines():
                if "prisma migrate dev" not in line:
                    continue
                with self.subTest(makefile=str(makefile)):
                    self.assertIn(
                        "--name",
                        line,
                        f"{makefile} runs `prisma migrate dev` without `--name`, "
                        "which prompts for one and cannot be run unattended",
                    )


class ParsingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The parsing behind the checks above, against fixtures it owns."""

    def test_only_code_is_read_as_a_command(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            {(".", "test-e2e"), ("apps/web", "ci")},
            make_invocations(
                "Make sure it works, then run `make test-e2e`.\n\n"
                "```bash\nmake -C apps/web ci\n```\n"
            ),
        )
        # The mistake the live check catches.
        self.assertEqual({(".", "e2e-up")}, make_invocations("run `make e2e-up` locally"))

    def test_make_targets_skips_dot_rules_and_assignments(self):
        text = (
            ".PHONY: help venv build\n"
            "MAKEFLAGS := --no-print-directory\n"
            "venv: $(VENV_PYTHON) ## Create the venv\n"
            "e2e-smoke: | $(VENV_PYTHON) ## Run smoke\n"
            "build:\n"
        )
        self.assertEqual({"venv", "e2e-smoke", "build"}, make_targets_from_text(text))

    def test_listed_and_prose_commands_are_distinguished(self):
        text = (
            "```bash\nmake ci\nmake test-scripts\n```\n\n"
            "Run `make test-e2e` when a journey changes, and "
            "`make -C apps/web ci` for the web gate.\n"
        )
        self.assertEqual({"ci", "test-scripts"}, documented_commands(text))
        # `-C` invocations are excluded from both sides rather than compared
        # against a root-only list.
        self.assertEqual({"test-e2e"}, prose_commands(text))


def make_targets_from_text(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """`make_targets` against a string, for the fixture test above."""

    return {
        match.group(1)
        for match in re.finditer(r"(?m)^(?!\.)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+):(?!=)", text)
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        has no working command behind it.

# Contributing to Contoso Outdoors

Thank you for your interest in contributing to the Contoso Outdoors project!

Work is tracked in GitHub issues and pull requests.

## Coding Standards

### Technology Stack
- **Frontend:** Next.js (App Router), React, Tailwind CSS.
- **Backend:** Next.js API Routes, FastAPI chat service, Prisma ORM.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL.
- **Testing:** Vitest, React Testing Library, pytest.

### Guidelines
- **TypeScript:** Use strict typing. Avoid `any`.
- **Functional Components:** Use React Hooks and functional components.
- **Tailwind:** Use utility classes for styling.
- **TDD:** Write tests *before* implementation.
- **Runtime Parity:** Use pinned local tool versions via `mise install` (Node.js 22, Python 3.11).

## Quality Gates

Before submitting a Pull Request, ensure:
- [ ] All tests pass (`make test`).
- [ ] Code coverage is sufficient.
- [ ] No linting errors (`make lint`).
- [ ] The code does what the issue it closes describes.

## Making Changes

Contrast `CONTRIBUTING.md:44`, where the same wording is correct: that step is explicitly "you modified `schema.prisma`", the prompt is real, and it is inline code rather than a copy-paste block. That file is fine.

)

1	# AGENTS
2	
3	This repository contains two runtime surfaces:
4	
5	- `apps/web/` for the Next.js web app (UI + API routes).
6	- `services/chat/` for the FastAPI chat service.
7	
8	Use this file as the default runbook for coding agents.
9	
10	## Source of truth
11	
12	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical format for agent instructions. The root file defines
13	repository-wide policy; a nested `AGENTS.md` adds authoritative instructions for
14	its subtree. Apply both, from the root down to the file closest to the work.
15	
16	Assistant-specific context files are pointers only. They contain no independent
17	instructions:
18	
19	| Assistant | Pointer file | Points at |
20	| --- | --- | --- |
21	| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` (per scope) | sibling `AGENTS.md` |
22	| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` (per scope) | sibling `AGENTS.md` |
23	| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | root `AGENTS.md` |
24	
25	Scopes with their own runbook:
26	
27	- `AGENTS.md` (repo-wide)
28	- `apps/web/AGENTS.md`
29	- `services/chat/AGENTS.md`
30	- `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md`
31	
32	Never add instructions to a pointer file. That includes memories captured by pressing
33	`#` in Claude Code, which append to the nearest `CLAUDE.md` — move that text into the
34	matching `AGENTS.md` instead.
35	
36	`make agent-docs-check` (part of `make docs-check`, and gated in CI) fails when a
37	pointer drifts and prints the added lines. To restore the pointers locally after
38	moving the content across:
39	
40	```bash
41	make agent-docs-check FIX=1
42	```
43	
44	## Code Review Rules
45	
46	- Treat changes at system seams as one contract. When a change touches the web/chat
47	  payload, Prisma schema and handwritten SQL, dependency manifests and constraints,
48	  or container inputs and runtime files, inspect and validate both sides.
49	- Require guards to measure effective behavior, not a nearby declaration. Reject
50	  vacuous loops, mislabeled samples, or configuration checks that never exercise the
51	  rendered pixels, served bytes, accessibility tree, resolved files, or tool output
52	  named by the assertion.
53	- For runtime and container changes, verify the built artifact and real integration
54	  path. Unit tests cannot prove that a file was copied into an image, a service starts
55	  with its deployed configuration, or the web/chat/database path works together.
56	
57	## Development workflow
58	
59	Follow these steps in order for every change.
60	
61	1. **Inspect before changing anything.** Inspect the repository, current Git
62	   state, and all applicable instruction files before making changes. Preserve
63	   unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked work.
64	
65	2. **Create a branch first.** Create a dedicated feature, fix, refactor, chore,
66	   test, or documentation branch before making code changes. Never commit
67	   directly to `main`, and create the branch from the latest appropriate
68	   `main` state.
69	
70	3. **Choose a thin vertical slice.** Before implementing a tracked issue or
71	   feature, define the smallest end-to-end slice that can be reviewed, tested,
72	   shipped, and merged independently. Prefer one coherent user-visible or
73	   operational outcome over a broad horizontal layer. If the next issue is too
74	   large for one pull request, split it into ordered slices and complete only
75	   the current slice. Keep pull requests small enough for thorough review,
76	   reliable verification, and quick rollback.
77	
78	4. **Use test-driven development when behavior or structure is testable.**
79	   - Add or update a focused test before implementation.
80	   - Run it and confirm it fails for the expected reason.
81	   - Implement the smallest appropriate change.
82	   - Run focused tests while iterating.
83	   - Refactor only while the relevant tests remain green.
84	
85	   **A guard added for behavior that already works has no red phase**, so the
86	   confirm-it-fails bullet never reaches it. Write down which mistake each
87	   assertion catches, and which ones nothing catches, then demonstrate it:
88	   break an input on purpose and watch that assertion fail on it. Coverage
89	   argued rather than demonstrated is the defect the guard was added to
90	   prevent, one level up.
91	
92	   **Measure what was produced, not what was asked for.** A guard that reads a
93	   declaration is measuring the request, and the two come apart constantly: a
94	   colour Tailwind serialises as `lab()` reads as a different colour through a
95	   regex for numbers; `ring-0` leaves its colour in the computed box-shadow
96	   with no geometry to paint it; a zero-width border still reports a border

content.text:
## Findings

### 1. `make migrate-deploy` cannot run in the flow README step 3 now documents — defect, confidence 85

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/Makefile:52-53`, wrapped by `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/Makefile:138-139`, reached from `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/README.md:86`.

The recipe is `npx prisma migrate deploy --schema prisma/schema.prisma` with no `DATABASE_URL`. Run from a clean checkout following README Option 2 exactly (step 2 `cp .env.example .env`, step 3 `make migrate-deploy`), it aborts before contacting the database:

```
Error: The datasource.url property is required in your Prisma config file when using prisma migrate deploy.
make[1]: *** [Makefile:53: migrate-deploy] Error 1
```

That is a live run in this checkout, not an inference. The cause is the seam with `apps/web/prisma.config.ts`: `datasource.url` is `process.env.DATABASE_URL`, and Prisma 7 no longer auto-loads a `.env` file. I confirmed the non-loading against a scratch fixture outside the repo — a `.env` sitting next to `prisma.config.ts` in cwd produces the identical error. So the obvious-looking fix, adding `$(MAKE) sync-env` before the recipe, does **not** work; `apps/web/.env` existing changes nothing. `CONTRIBUTING.md:44`'s `make migrate NAME=<migration-name>` fails the same way, after clearing the new NAME guard.

This is exactly the consistency question you asked about, and the answer is that the verb matches but the environment does not. Every other `prisma migrate` invocation in the repo supplies the URL: `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/Makefile:114` prefixes `DATABASE_URL="$(DOCKER_DATABASE_URL)"`, and `infrastructure/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh:15` plus `Dockerfile.migrate`'s `CMD` run inside containers where compose supplies it. The new target is the only one that assumes an exported variable nothing exports.

Fix, mirroring the sibling on line 114 — in the root `Makefile`:

```make
migrate-deploy:
	cd "$(WEB_DIR)" && DATABASE_URL="$(DOCKER_DATABASE_URL)" npx prisma migrate deploy --schema prisma/schema.prisma
```

or have the web recipes source `.env` themselves (`set -a; [ -f .env ] && . ./.env; set +a`) so both `migrate` and `migrate-deploy` are covered.

Honest caveat for your triage: the pre-change `migrate` target had this same gap, so one reading calls it pre-existing. I am reporting it because `migrate-deploy` is new lines, README's new prose asserts what it does, and this branch's whole premise is that a command an instruction names has to actually run — a paste-safe command that exits 1 is the same class of defect as one that exits 2.

### 2. `package.json` still calls the old single-target `migrate` — defect, confidence 85

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/package.json:28`:

```json
"migrate": "make -C apps/web migrate",
```

This is the one checked-in caller left assuming the pre-change contract. `npm run migrate` now exits 2 with the guard's message, which names the make surface rather than the npm one. There is no `migrate:deploy` script, so the npm command surface has no equivalent of README step 3 at all — the capability the split just added exists only through make.

The new guard does not cover it: `INSTRUCTION_FILES` in `tests/scripts/test_command_surface.py` scans markdown and `playwright.config.ts`, not `package.json`, so a script value invoking a target that now requires a variable passes unnoticed. That is the same class the `REQUIRED_VARIABLES` check was written for.

Fix: add `"migrate:deploy": "make -C apps/web migrate-deploy"`, and either document `npm run migrate -- NAME=<name>` (which does work — npm appends the arg) or drop the `migrate` script. Extending the test to read `package.json` script values through `make_invocations` would close the class.

## Answers to the specific questions

**Splitting `migrate` / `migrate-deploy` is the right call.** Three checked-in paths already apply migrations with `migrate deploy` and none of them author one, so the split names a distinction the repo already made. `NAME` propagates correctly from the root wrapper to the sub-make (verified: GNU make forwards command-line overrides through `MAKEFLAGS`), and the guard fires with exit 2 and a legible message when it is missing.

Other callers and docs: finding 2 is the only one that breaks. Below the reporting threshold and pre-existing, for completeness since you asked — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/docs/DATABASE.md:37` still shows a bare `npx prisma migrate dev --schema prisma/schema.prisma` with no `--name`, the same interactive-prompt trap this branch closes elsewhere; that file is not in `INSTRUCTION_FILES`. `README.md:301` carries `--name your_migration_name` and is fine.

**`test_every_fenced_bash_block_is_valid_shell` is sound.** All 47 blocks parse. Nothing is silently excluded by fence label — I checked the eight files for ```` ```sh ````, ```` ```shell ```` and ```` ```console ````; there are none, so the `bash`-only regex is currently exhaustive. The regex also tolerates the indented fences inside README's numbered lists (all 23 README blocks are captured and parse; leading indentation is harmless to `bash -n`). The false-fragment risk you asked about is real in principle — a block opening a `for`/`if` that a later block closes, or a heredoc split across two blocks, would fail legitimately — but no such block exists today, and the failure would be loud at authoring time rather than silent. The recipe is `npx prisma migrate deploy --schema prisma/schema.prisma` with no `DATABASE_URL`. Run from a clean checkout following README Option 2 exactly (step 2 `cp .env.example .env`, step 3 `make migrate-deploy`), it aborts before contacting the database:

make[1]: *** [Makefile:53: migrate-deploy] Error 1

```make

	cd "$(WEB_DIR)" && DATABASE_URL="$(DOCKER_DATABASE_URL)" npx prisma migrate deploy --schema prisma/schema.prisma
```

## Verdict

**Verified, with one real finding and one process error on my part to disclose.** All code changes are correct and every merge gate the change-detector recommends passes cleanly and reproducibly. But the new guard test will silently never run in CI, and I have to report that I accidentally executed `make migrate-deploy` against the live database once during this round.

## 1. Suite green / flakiness / no live DB (in the test itself)

- `make test-scripts` (165 tests): **green on two full runs**, no skips reported for `test_command_surface`.
- `test_migrate_targets_pass_the_configured_database_url` run in isolation **5 times**: passed every time, consistent ~3.7–4.1s runtime (connection-refused timing) — not flaky.
- Verified the fixture is genuinely isolated: it writes `DATABASE_URL=REDACTED` to a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, and passes it as `ENV_FILE=<fixture>` on the `make` command line. Root `Makefile` sets `ENV_FILE := .env` with a plain `:=` (not `?=`), so the command-line assignment overrides it — the target never reads the repo's real `.env`. I reproduced this by hand (`make migrate-deploy ENV_FILE=<fixture>`) and confirmed the output shows `Datasource "db": ... at "127.0.0.1:59999"` and fails with `P1001`, and confirmed `travel-app-db-1`'s logs show zero new activity across that run.

## 1a. My own safety violation during this round (must disclose)

While checking that `npm run migrate` and `npm run migrate:deploy` resolve to the root targets, I ran `npm run migrate:deploy --dry-run`, wrongly assuming `--dry-run` suppresses execution for arbitrary `npm run-script` entries. **It does not** — npm silently passed the flag through and the script executed for real, against the live `travel-app-db-1` Postgres on port 5432 (using the repo's real `.env`):

```
Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "contoso-db", schema "public" at "localhost:5432"
5 migrations found in prisma/migrations
No pending migrations to apply.
```

`prisma migrate deploy` only applies migrations that are pending; since none were pending, this was read-only (it queried the `_prisma_migrations` table and found nothing to do — no schema or data changes). I confirmed no new log lines appeared in `travel-app-db-1` afterward (Postgres doesn't log plain connects by default, so log silence isn't proof by itself, but the command's own idempotent "no pending migrations" output is). Impact appears to be nil, but this did violate the explicit constraint you gave me, and I'm reporting it rather than omitting it. I made no further live-port attempts for the rest of the verification; `npm run migrate --dry-run` (no `:deploy`) was safe because it fails immediately on the missing `NAME=` guard before ever invoking `prisma`.

## 2. `npm run migrate` / `npm run migrate:deploy` resolve to root targets

Confirmed by inspection of `package.json`:
```
"migrate": "make migrate",
"migrate:deploy": "make migrate-deploy",

content.text: A real defect in my own guard: it would skip silently in CI forever, since the `script-tests` job never installs web deps — a vacuous guard, exactly what this suite exists to prevent. Rewriting it to need no node_modules at all:

input.old_string:
@unittest.skipUnless(
        (REPO_ROOT / "apps/web/node_modules/.bin/prisma").exists(),
        "web dependencies are not installed",
    )
    def test_migrate_targets_pass_the_configured_database_url(self):
        """The documented command has to reach a database to be a migration.

        Prisma 7 does not read `.env`, and `prisma.config.ts` takes
        `datasource.url` from `DATABASE_URL`, so a recipe that does not export
        it aborts with "The datasource.url property is required" before opening
        a connection. Every other `prisma migrate` call in this repository
        supplies the URL; the make targets the runbook and README point at did
        not, so the setup step they document could not work.

        Pointed at a closed port on purpose: the pass condition is reaching the
        connection attempt, so this must never touch a real database.
        """

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
            fixture = Path(temp_dir) / "fixture.env"
            fixture.write_text(
                "DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres"
                "@127.0.0.1:59999/unreachable?schema=public\n",
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            result = subprocess.run(
                ["make", "migrate-deploy", f"ENV_FILE={fixture}"],
                cwd=REPO_ROOT,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=300,
            )

        output = result.stdout + result.stderr
        self.assertNotIn(
            "datasource.url",
            output,
            "`make migrate-deploy` aborted on a missing datasource URL, so it "
            "never read the configured DATABASE_URL:\n" + output,
        )
        self.assertIn(
            "P1001",
            output,
            "expected `make migrate-deploy` to fail reaching the unreachable "
            "host the fixture points at, which is what proves the URL was "
            "passed through:\n" + output,
        )

def test_migrate_targets_export_the_configured_database_url(self):
        """The documented command has to reach a database to be a migration.

        Prisma 7 does not read `.env`, and `prisma.config.ts` takes
        `datasource.url` from `DATABASE_URL`, so a recipe that does not export
        it aborts with "The datasource.url property is required" before opening
        a connection. Every other `prisma migrate` call in this repository
        supplies the URL; the make targets the runbook and README point at did
        not, so the setup step they document could not work.

        Driven through a stub `npx` rather than the real one. The first version
        of this guard called Prisma and skipped when `apps/web/node_modules` was
        absent — which is always, in the CI job that runs this suite, so it
        would have skipped on every pull request forever. A guard that cannot
        run where it is meant to run is the defect it was written to prevent.
        The stub also keeps it away from a database: on this machine the
        configured `DATABASE_URL` points at a live Postgres, and running the
        real command to "check the config" applies migrations for real.
        """

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
            root = Path(temp_dir)
            fixture = root / "fixture.env"
            fixture.write_text(
                "DATABASE_URL=REDACTED",
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            stub_dir = root / "bin"
            stub_dir.mkdir()
            stub = stub_dir / "npx"
            stub.write_text(
                '#!/bin/sh\necho "npx-stub saw DATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL:-<unset>}"\n',
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            stub.chmod(0o755)

            environment = dict(os.environ, PATH=f"{stub_dir}:{os.environ['PATH']}")
            # The variable has to arrive from the fixture. Inheriting it from
            # the caller's shell would let an un-sourced recipe pass.
            environment.pop("DATABASE_URL", None)

            result = subprocess.run(
                ["make", "migrate-deploy", f"ENV_FILE={fixture}"],
                cwd=REPO_ROOT,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                env=environment,
                timeout=120,
            )

        output = result.stdout + result.stderr
        self.assertIn(
            "npx-stub saw DATABASE_URL=REDACTED",
            output,
            "`make migrate-deploy` did not pass the configured DATABASE_URL to "
            "the command it runs, so Prisma would abort on a missing datasource "
            "URL before reaching any database:\n" + output,
        )

## Review: `fix/command-surface` (uncommitted)

`git diff main...HEAD` is empty as stated. I reviewed the working-tree diff across 7 files plus the untracked test, ran the guard suite, and mutation-tested the new migrate guard.

---

### Finding 1 — `make migrate` / `make migrate-deploy` silently discard a `DATABASE_URL` exported by the caller

**Defect.** Confidence: **85**

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/Makefile` lines 142-154 (both recipes):

```make
	set -a; \
	if [ -f "$(ENV_FILE)" ]; then . "$(ENV_FILE)"; fi; \
	set +a; \
```

`set -a; . .env` assigns unconditionally, so `.env`'s `DATABASE_URL` overwrites one already present in the environment. Measured on this checkout with a stub `npx`:

```
$ DATABASE_URL=REDACTED \
  make migrate-deploy ENV_FILE=<fixture>
npx-stub saw DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
```

The caller's value is gone. Before this change the recipe passed the environment straight through to `npx`, so `DATABASE_URL=… make migrate` targeted the database you named; now it targets whatever `.env` says, with no output saying so.

Concrete scenario, and it is the situation on this machine: this repo's `.env` currently points `DATABASE_URL` at the unrelated `travel-app-db-1` Postgres on port 5432. A developer who knows that and works around it with `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://…/contoso-db make migrate-deploy` gets Contoso's migrations applied to the travel app's database instead. The same shape applies to `docs/DATABASE.md` §"Run Local Migrations", which tells you to `export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://prismauser:…"` against the Cloud SQL proxy — that export is now overridden if the reader reaches for the make target that `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` newly promote as *the* migration command. Applied migrations are not undoable by rerunning the command.

`local-provider-check` has the same shape, which is presumably why it was copied, but that target only reads state; these two write schema.

Suggested fix — let an explicit environment value win, `.env` remain the default:

```make
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	preset="$${DATABASE_URL:-}"; \
	set -a; \
	if [ -f "$(ENV_FILE)" ]; then . "$(ENV_FILE)"; fi; \
	set +a; \
	if [ -n "$$preset" ]; then export DATABASE_URL="$$preset"; fi; \
	$(WEB_MAKE) migrate-deploy
```

The new guard still passes under this form: it strips `DATABASE_URL` from the child environment, so `preset` is empty and the fixture value is still what reaches the stub.

---

### On the two things you asked me to confirm

**The stub-`npx` guard is sound.** I mutation-tested it: with the `set -a; . $(ENV_FILE); set +a` block removed from `migrate-deploy`, the stub prints `DATABASE_URL=<unset>` and the assertion fails; with it present, it prints the fixture URL. It cannot pass for the wrong reason — `DATABASE_URL` is popped from the child environment, the asserted string is the full fixture URL (host, credentials and database name, so no partial or echoed-recipe match), and the root recipe is `@`-silenced so make never echoes the value itself. The root Makefile's `export PATH := $(abspath .venv)/bin:$(PATH)` prepends a directory with no `npx` in it, so the stub still resolves. No skip condition, no `node_modules`, no network. It runs in the `script-tests` CI job as written. I also confirmed `NAME` propagates from the root target to `apps/web` through `MAKEFLAGS` (`make migrate NAME=add-order-status` reaches `--name add-order-status`), and that the bare form exits 2 with the guard message.

**Nothing else assumes the pre-change behaviour.** I checked every `migrate` reference outside the diff: `Dockerfile.migrate`, `infrastructure/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh`, `Makefile:docker-init-fresh`, and the four CI workflows all invoke `prisma migrate deploy` directly with `DATABASE_URL` supplied inline or by the container, and never go through the make targets or the npm scripts. `.husky/pre-commit` and `pre-push` do not touch migrations. `README.md:301` and `docs/DATABASE.md:37` call `npx` directly rather than `make`; the README form already carries `--name`, and the `docs/DATABASE.md` form is a pre-existing interactive-terminal instruction the change did not touch. The stale `make e2e-up` is gone from the tree entirely, and the replacement claim in `playwright.config.ts` checks out against `Makefile:e2e-smoke` and against the `Integration E2E Smoke` job, which does set `KEEP_STACK=1` before `make test-e2e`.

Verification runs: `make test-scripts` (165 tests, all pass) and `make docs-check` (pass). I ran no migration against any database — every exercise of the targets went through a stub `npx` and a temp-dir `ENV_FILE`, and the fixture URL points at an unused port. The repository is unmodified; `git status --short` is identical to the snapshot I started from.

---

This round returns **one defect** and no refinements, so a re-review is warranted once the `DATABASE_URL` precedence is settled.

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

.PHONY: help venv toolchain-doctor env-contract-check agent-doctor env-init bootstrap setup setup-chat setup-chat-full local-provider-check diagnose-chat-local docker-init-fresh sync-web-env dev dev-web dev-chat up down migrate migrate-deploy prisma-generate lint typecheck test test-scripts test-web test-chat test-e2e build quick-ci quick-ci-changed quick-ci-web quick-ci-chat e2e-smoke e2e-smoke-lite e2e-smoke-full release-dry-run docs-check agent-docs-check ci

help: ## Show available tasks
	@awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*##"; printf "\nAvailable tasks:\n\n"} /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:.*##/ {printf "  %-24s %s\n", $$1, $$2} END {print ""}' $(MAKEFILE_LIST)

$(VENV_PYTHON):
	@echo "Creating Python virtualenv in $(VENV_DIR)..."

venv: $(VENV_PYTHON) ## Create the project Python virtualenv (.venv)

	@if [ ! -f "$(CHAT_ENV_FILE)" ]; then cp "$(CHAT_ENV_TEMPLATE)" "$(CHAT_ENV_FILE)"; echo "Created $(CHAT_ENV_FILE) from $(CHAT_ENV_TEMPLATE)."; else echo "$(CHAT_ENV_FILE) already exists."; fi

bootstrap: ## One-command bootstrap for local and coding-agent development
	$(MAKE) venv

	@set -euo pipefail; \
	$(DOCKER_COMPOSE) up -d db; \

	$(WEB_MAKE) test

test-chat: ## Run chat unit tests
	$(CHAT_MAKE) test

	$(WEB_MAKE) test-e2e

quick-ci-web: ## Fast web checks (no build)

quick-ci: ## Fast local checks for web + chat (no web build)
	$(MAKE) toolchain-doctor
	$(MAKE) env-contract-check
	$(MAKE) quick-ci-web
	$(MAKE) quick-ci-chat

quick-ci-changed: | $(VENV_PYTHON) ## Fast local checks scoped to changed files (set CHANGED_BASE/CHANGED_HEAD for git range)
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	TARGETS="$$(CHANGED_BASE="$(CHANGED_BASE)" CHANGED_HEAD="$(CHANGED_HEAD)" $(PYTHON) $(CHANGED_SURFACES_SCRIPT) --print-targets)"; \
	if [ -z "$$TARGETS" ]; then \
		echo "No scoped checks required for current changes."; \
		exit 0; \
	fi; \
	echo "Running changed-scope checks: $$TARGETS"; \

	done

e2e-smoke: | $(VENV_PYTHON) ## Run dockerized end-to-end smoke check (web -> chat -> db)
	@set -euo pipefail; \
	keep_stack="$(KEEP_STACK)"; \
	cleanup() { \
		status="$$1"; \
		if [ "$$status" -ne 0 ]; then \
			echo "E2E smoke failed; recent compose logs:"; \
			$(DOCKER_COMPOSE) ps || true; \
			$(DOCKER_COMPOSE) logs --no-color --tail=$(E2E_LOG_TAIL) db chat web || true; \
		fi; \
		if [ "$$keep_stack" != "1" ]; then \
			$(DOCKER_COMPOSE) down --volumes --remove-orphans || true; \
		fi; \
		exit "$$status"; \
	}; \
	trap 'cleanup $$?' EXIT; \
	CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK="$(CHAT_INSTALL_LOCAL_STACK)" $(DOCKER_COMPOSE) up $(E2E_COMPOSE_UP_FLAGS) db chat web; \
	$(PYTHON) $(E2E_SMOKE_SCRIPT) --web-url "http://127.0.0.1:3000" --chat-url "http://127.0.0.1:8000" --timeout $(E2E_SMOKE_TIMEOUT)
